title: Suspend, reactivate and purge a tenant: the operator deactivates and reactivates the fixture tenant; unknown tenants and company users are refused
description: The platform administrator deactivates the fixture tenant (200, status inactive), sees it inactive, deactivates it again (a no-op, still 200), reactivates it (200, active) and again (no-op). A deactivate or reactivate of an unknown slug answers 404 and changes nothing; a company administrator's deactivate and purge are refused. The cleanup reactivates the fixture so it ends active. NOT automated, on purpose: (1) the deactivate of the platform tenant itself (the guard answers 409; a failing guard would take the platform down, the guard is covered by test/letflow/routers/tenants_test.exs); (2) the sign-in refusal of a deactivated tenant's users (tenant_inactive 403) because the fixture has no user; (3) the purge step s10: not runnable on QA, no lifecycle row for uat-tmp tenants (infra 2026-11-21), written blocked_by qa-provisioner-config until the provisioner window. The platform fixture tenant uat-tmp-fixture (looked up, or created with --allow-create, by the first four steps f1..f4 of this file) is the only tenant these steps touch; it is created once, never purged (QA cannot purge it) and never counts as residue; the process leaves it in the known state: active, no host name, platform kill switch off, solo audit not allowed. While the fixture does not exist on QA (the case on 2026-11-25) every step that needs it is SKIPPED with the log note 'requires fixture_id' and the run passes on the fixture-free steps only: a PASS then says nothing about the fixture steps. The first run with --allow-create creates the fixture; from then on the steps run.

steps.says: Look for the fixture tenant by its fixed slug (404 is an answer, not a failure).
Create it only when absent (the run must be started with --allow-create; without the flag the step is skipped with that reason).
Wait until the tenant exists (the registration process creates it in the background).
Known state: active. Reactivating an active tenant is a no-op that answers 200.
The operator reads the fixture tenant: it is active.
The operator deactivates it: 200 and the status is inactive.
A second deactivate is a no-op that still answers 200 (OQ-2 of the tenants router).
The operator reactivates it: 200 and active again.
A second reactivate is a no-op that answers 200.
An unknown slug cannot be deactivated: 404, nothing changes.
An unknown slug cannot be reactivated: 404.
A company administrator is refused the deactivate of the fixture tenant (403 or the uniform 404).
Purge of an ACTIVE tenant is refused: 409 not_eligible, nothing is deleted.
A company administrator is refused the purge route (403 or the uniform 404).
Final check: the fixture is active again.

cleanup.says: Cleanup: reactivate the fixture whatever happened (a no-op when it is active).
